thread:
alex: Heads-up: were expecting our kiddo in mid-July. I'm thinking of starting leave the week prior and taking ~10 weeks after. Who should I notify, and what paperwork/benefit steps do I need to take so pay and health coverage are smooth?

priya: Congrats @alex! :party_popper: Best practice: 1) Submit a parental leave request in the HR portal once you have an approximate date (we ask for ~30 days notice when possible). 2) If eligible, file FMLA/CFRA (or local equivalent) for job protection. 3) Open a short-term disability (STD) claim if your state/employer STD applies  that covers part of pay; Redwood has a company top-up for primary caregivers (see below). 4) Add baby to benefits within 30 days. I'll DM the links and the checklist.

alex: Awesome, thanks. Is the top-up automatic? Also what about payroll timing?

jamie: The top-up is handled by payroll but requires the STD claim to be submitted and company leave request approved. For primary caregivers: Redwood pays 8 weeks at 100% salary from company funds. After that, you can bridge remaining weeks using PTO or combine with state benefits; payroll will coordinate. Non-primary caregivers get 4 weeks at 100%. Payroll note: to make sure payments hit the expected paycheck, submit requests and STD confirmation at least 10 business days ahead of payroll cutoff (cutoff is the 1st of each month for that month's pay).

morgan: For documentation: physicians note with expected due date for birth, or placement docs for adoption. FMLA forms if applicable, and confirmation from the STD carrier. If you're outside the US, there are different statutory rules  ping me with your country and I'll confirm details.

alex: I'm on the UK payroll, actually. Anything different I should do?

morgan: For UK teammates, statutory maternity/paternity pay rules apply. We offer a company top-up for eligible employees similar to the US policy, but timing and forms differ. I'll follow up DM with the local HR packet and the process for SMP/SAP.

ben: Ops/coverage: alex, can you draft a 1-page handoff with your weeklies, critical endpoints, and PRs that need owning while you're OOO? Also list a 2-week overlap window for ramp-down and ramp-up so we can schedule a contractor if needed. For alerts: add an "alerts & escalation" section in the runbook with pagerduty names and basic remediation steps.

alex: Will do. For the contractor, whats the usual turnaround from request to start?

ben: If you use our vendor bench it's typically 1-2 weeks. If we post publicly it can be longer. Include required skills, hourly band, dates, and a short onboarding plan in the req. People Ops can fast-track vendor use for short parental covers.

priya: HR checklist for you: 
- Submit parental leave request in portal
- File STD claim with insurer after you have the due date
- Submit FMLA/CFRA/local leave paperwork if you want job protection
- Add dependent to benefits within 30 days of birth
- If you need caregiver top-up, indicate primary caregiver status in the request

hr-bot: AUTOMATED: "Parental leave request received for alex (thread 1719051234). Please upload supporting docs: physician's due date confirmation, STD claim number, and dependent documentation after birth."

alex: Uploaded initial leave request and a rough runbook. I'll add the alerts section and a list of active tickets. Thanks all.

priya: Happy to run a 20-min walkthrough of the portal if you want tomorrow morning. Congrats again!

alex: That would be great, thanks :heart:
